This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0e6c56198038b8f649dcfdcc1fe7005f6e804025` — the merge of head `bb52af6b1e75909390943f83ca77183a3db81fec` into base `385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0e6c56198038b8f649dcfdcc1fe7005f6e804025 && git checkout 0e6c56198038b8f649dcfdcc1fe7005f6e804025
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca bb52af6b1e75909390943f83ca77183a3db81fec && git checkout -B drift-repro 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca && git merge --no-ff bb52af6b1e75909390943f83ca77183a3db81fec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bb52af6b1e75909390943f83ca77183a3db81fec`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. The `--modes` value `ask` is new (`cli.ts`). The mode union widens to `'scratch' | 'template' | 'ask'` on `RunOptions.modes`, `ModeRun.mode`, `modeDir`, `StepRef.mode` (so an external driver's `step.mode` may now read `ask`, which the line names), `ModeScorecard.mode` and `CliArgs.modes`. New on `./runner`: export `askModeRefusal` and optional `ModeScorecard.supplied`. New on `./export`: the record reader's `mode` enum accepts `ask`, export `ASK_MODE_NOT_EXPORTED` and optional `Transcript.notShown`. No existing export is removed or narrowed.

The answer that moves is declared and is confined to runs that ask for `ask`. `templateMode`'s install is factored into `withInstalledBuild` with no change in order or recorded fields; the host directory is still `modeDir(card, 'template')` for template mode. Ask mode installs the same verified build (supplied `--template`, else this run's passing scratch build), runs `runHalf` under `card/ask/run/…` with `--ask-repeats` honoured, and never calls `driver.author`. It passes the verified artifact itself as `runHalf`'s `built`, the same artifact scratch mode's first Run half reads when the build is this run's, so on one build and one set of turns the grades agree (pinned, a wrong answer and a leak included, and under `recorded:`). `ask` with neither `--template` nor `scratch` is refused at parse and again in `runCard`. The exporter reads a record holding an ask mode, neither judges it nor shows its turns, and says why; it never refuses the record over it. Default modes are byte-identical in record, scorecard and export (pinned).

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, app metadata or card JSON changes. The widening is additive union members, exports and optional fields of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. No grader verdict moves: the ask mode's turns are graded by the unchanged `gradeCardAnswer`, and the gallery's pass rule for scratch and template is unchanged.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-4nulzg`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
